{"filepath":"clarifying_questions.md","content":"Clarifying questions — “Make it better” project

Please answer the questions below as specifically as you can. Your answers will let us scope work, identify quick wins, and produce an actionable plan.

1) What exactly should we "make better"?
- What is the object: product, service, document, codebase, process, campaign, design, or other? Give the name and short description.
- Who are the primary users or stakeholders?

2) Current pain points
- What problems or frustrations are you seeing now? List the top 3–5 pain points with brief examples or screenshots if possible.

3) Desired outcome and success metrics
- What does “better” look like? Describe concrete outcomes (e.g., fewer support tickets, faster load time, higher conversion rate, clearer approvals).
- What measurable metrics will indicate success and any target numbers or percentage improvements?

4) Constraints and non-negotiables
- Timeline: any hard deadlines or milestone dates?
- Budget: approximate budget or resource limits (e.g., team hours, tools, external spend)?
- Platform/tech constraints: tech stack, browsers, device targets, integrations, compliance or security rules?
- Access: who can provide access to systems, repos, analytics, or stakeholders? Do we have credentials or will you grant them?

5) Existing materials to review
- Please list or attach relevant files, links, repos, tickets, analytics dashboards, design files, or documentation. Preferable formats or places to look (Google Drive, GitHub, Figma, Notion, Jira). Include any passwords or access instructions if needed.

6) Priority areas
- If we can only address 1–2 things in the first sprint, what should they be? (e.g., stability, conversion funnel, user onboarding, code quality)
- Are there any areas to avoid or deprioritize now?

7) Risks and dependencies
- Known risks, open dependencies, or external teams we must coordinate with?

8) Communication and approvals
- Who will be the main point of contact (name, role, best contact method)?
- Who has final sign-off on changes?
- Preferred frequency and format for updates (daily standup, weekly report, Slack messages, demo)?

9) Preferred timeline for initial engagement
- When can you provide answers and materials? When would you like an initial plan or estimate (e.g., 48–72 hours, 1 week)?

Optional: examples or inspirations
- Are there examples (competitors, products, designs) you want us to emulate or avoid? Links are helpful.

Recommended next-step sequence for our team after you reply
1) Intake & access (24–48 hours)
   - Confirm receipt of your answers and gather files/credentials.
   - Schedule a short kickoff call (15–30 min) if needed to clarify ambiguities.
2) Rapid review & triage (48–72 hours)
   - Team specialists (product, UX, engineering, QA) review materials and map pain points to possible solutions.
   - Identify 1–3 quick wins and estimate effort.
3) Prioritize & propose plan (3–5 business days)
   - Present proposed scope, success metrics, timeline, and cost/effort estimate.
   - Get sign-off on priorities and constraints.
4) Sprint execution (per agreed cadence)
   - Execute work in short iterations (1–2 week sprints) with demos and feedback loops.
   - Track progress against agreed metrics.
5) Validate & iterate
   - Measure results, collect stakeholder feedback, and plan follow-up improvements.

If you want, answer the numbered questions directly in reply or attach a completed copy of this file. If you're short on time, tell us the top 3 facts (what to improve, biggest pain, deadline) and we will start with a high-level discovery.

Thank you — we’ll convert your answers into a prioritized plan and next steps."}
function.name: write_file
